_comment: Settings for the clean and blend steps (python -m processing.run). Temperatures in degrees C, salinity in PSU, distances in km.

grid._comment: Output grid: the area bbox in config/area.json, in cells of cell_deg_lat x cell_deg_lon (about 500 m x 500 m at 26 N). The compute grid adds pad cells to the north and west so the COMPS C10 and C12 edge anchors connect by water. Water paths are traced on a fine mask fine_factor times finer (about 100 m), so narrow rivers stay open and thin barrier islands stay closed. Stations off the mask snap to mapped tidal water within station_snap_km, or are left out of the grids.
grid._barriers_comment: Structures that separate tidal from fresh water. The water mask is cut within radius_m of each point (python -m processing.shoreline), so water above them drops out of the grids.

barriers.name: S-79 W.P. Franklin Lock and Dam, Caloosahatchee

qc._comment: Tests follow the IOOS QARTOD manuals. Flags: 1 good, 3 suspect, 4 bad. Suspect and bad readings are left out of the hourly values and the blend. Each run re-checks the last rewrite_days days, reading context_days more before them.

bottom_temperature._comment: Where a station has no near-surface sensor, its mid or bottom temperature feeds the temperature grid if the water there is no deeper than max_depth_m (NOAA Coastal Relief Model, processing/depths.py). Never used for salinity.

merge._comment: Stations flagged possible_duplicate_of, or within max_distance_m of each other, are merged into one physical station only if their readings agree: median absolute difference over at least min_overlap_hours shared hours no more than water_temp_c / salinity_psu. Otherwise both stay.

qc._gross_range_comment: Salinity and conductance limits sit well above Florida Bay's records so hypersaline water is kept: USGS Florida Bay gauges peaked at 60 PSU and 84,500 uS/cm (McCormick Creek, July 2015, the seagrass die-off), and 64.4 PSU was reported in July 2015. 80 and 100 PSU correspond to about 108,000 and 130,000 uS/cm (PSS-78 extrapolated, as USGS does above 42).

spike._comment: A reading is a spike when it sits further than the threshold from the median of readings within window_minutes either side, and further than mad_factor times their scaled median absolute deviation.

flatline._comment: Identical readings for this many hours. Below the surface the hours are multiplied by below_surface_factor; thermistor strings are not tested. Salinity runs below fresh_floor_psu are skipped, and so are runs where the station's conductance keeps changing, because both come from rounding, not a stuck sensor.

neighbor._comment: Temperature only. A station whose hourly readings stay more than this many degrees from the median of stations within max_km by water path, over a rolling window_hours window, is flagged suspect. Salinity is skipped: real salinity differences between nearby estuary sites are large.

stale._comment: A station is stale when its newest reading is older than default_hours plus the provider's normal delay plus two reporting intervals.

hourly._comment: Hourly value = mean of good readings within half_window_minutes of the hour.

blend._comment: Each run re-blends any hour in the last reblend_hours whose inputs changed, and fills any hour missing from the last backfill_days. GOES-19 values are carried forward up to goes_persistence_days.

temperature._comment: Optimal interpolation of sensor-minus-satellite corrections. Correlation falls off as (1 + d/L) exp(-d/L) with water-path distance d and L = length_km. Background error grows with the age of the satellite value and with water-path distance from the nearest satellite pixel (sqrt(sat_error^2 + (age_error_per_hour * age)^2 + (extension_error_per_km * km)^2), capped). Water the satellite never sees fades from the nearest satellite value into a regional mean of the sensors over extension_blend_km of water path (regional mean as for salinity). Values fitted to the Nov 11-14 2026 data by leave-one-out (processing/validate.py). Confidence is 100 * (1 - error / confidence_error_scale), floored at 0.

salinity._comment: Sensors only. Background: Gulf salinity (median of stations at least offshore_km from land, else gulf_default_psu) in open water, fading over sea_blend_km of water path into a regional field (Gaussian weights over regional_length_km; stations closer than declutter_km to each other share weight). Optimal interpolation then adds detail within about length_km of each sensor. Confidence is 100 * (1 - error / confidence_error_scale).
